title: Perseid Meteor Showers & Science in Quran
description:
Every August, the skies light up with the Perseid meteor showers, caused by debris from the Swift–Tuttle comet burning in Earth’s atmosphere. Modern science can predict their exact timing, intensity, and visibility — but what did people think 1,400 years ago?

According to the Quran (Ayah 6:10) and Hadith (Sahih Muslim 26:5538), meteors are not cosmic dust but weapons thrown by Allah at djinns who try to eavesdrop on heavenly councils. In this video from Pale Blue Thoughts, we explain how the Quran and tafsirs by Al-Bukhari, Muslim, and Ibn Majah describe meteors as “shooting stars” used against devils — a claim still defended by Islamic apologetics.

Science, however, tells us meteors are small fragments of rock and ice ignited by friction in Earth’s atmosphere. The Perseids, peaking around August 12–13, can produce up to 100 shooting stars per hour, best viewed away from city lights and near the constellation Perseus. Tools like SkyView Lite, Stellarium, and Night Sky Tracker can help you spot them.

This video contrasts religion vs astronomy, showing how ancient myths misrepresent natural phenomena. From calling meteors “signs from God” to modern apologists painting scripture as science, this is a clear case where faith fails and science shines.

👉 If you’ve searched for Perseid meteor shower, Perseids 2023, Quran meteors djinns, Islamic view meteors, shooting stars religion, Allah throws stars, Perseid meteor science explained — this video gives you the scientific perspective.
